transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-01
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 00:52:00
Attendees: Ava Mercer (Redwood AE); Diego Ruiz (Redwood SE); Priya Shah (Redwood CSM); Dr. Elena Ortiz (CTO, Hawthorn); Marcus Lee (Head of Infrastructure); Sofia Kim (Compliance Manager); Evan Park (DevOps)

Summary: Quick discovery on security posture and data residency needs for potential Private or Dedicated deployment. Customer emphasized PHI handling, SOC2/ISO requirements, strict retention and KMS controls, and desire to run inference in a VPC with customer-managed keys.

Topics: SOC2 / ISO certifications, SSO/SAML and RBAC, audit logs retention and export, encryption/KMS (BYOK), data residency and on-prem vs VPC, model hosting tradeoffs (hosted vs dedicated vs private), compliance timelines.

Action items (recap at end included in metadata)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're on for 50 minutes — does that still work?
[00:08] Elena (Hawthorn CTO): Yep, works for me. We've got about 45 minutes but that's fine.
[00:12] Ava: Great. Quick intros — I'm Ava, AE at Redwood, Diego is our solutions engineer, Priya is our CSM. Could each of you do a one-liner on your role?
[00:20] Elena: I'm Elena, CTO at Hawthorn MedTech, we build diagnostic tooling that touches PHI.
[00:25] Marcus: Marcus, I run infra and cloud ops. We're evaluating where inference will run and what the security gates are.
[00:30] Sofia: Sofia, compliance — mainly focused on data residency, retention, and auditability.
[00:34] Evan: Evan, devops, will be hands-on for deployments and keys.
[00:37] Diego (Redwood SE): Thanks all. High level we'll walk through our hosted, dedicated, and private options and focus on the security controls that matter.

[00:46] Elena: The reason we're here — the board and legal have asked for clear answers on: Can we keep PHI on-prem or in a VPC? Is BYOK possible? How long are logs kept and can we get them for audits?
[00:58] Ava: Absolutely. High level: Redwood Hosted gives fastest time to value but has shared infra; Dedicated reserves GPU pools for you in our cloud with isolation; Private gives you customer-controlled network and optionally on-prem. For PHI, many customers choose Dedicated with strict network egress rules or Private (VPC or on-prem) when they need full control.

[01:20] Marcus: Can you confirm whether Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSMs? We cannot have keys we don't control for PHI decryption at rest.
[01:28] Diego: Yes — Private supports BYOK integrations with major cloud KMS and also HSM chaining for on-prem. We have doc links — I'll share the KMS integration pattern. Note: there was a minor mise-label in the cert doc where K V cash was spelled weird in an earlier draft — sorry, auto transcript mess.

[01:45] Sofia: Also need to know SOC2 and ISO status. If you can't provide SOC2 Type II then we'll need alternative mitigations.
[01:53] Ava: We are SOC2 Type II certified; we also have an ISO 27001 audit in our roadmap — will send the cert.

[02:02] Elena: Great. For SSO, we're on Okta. Does Redwood support SAML or SCIM for provisioning?
[02:09] Diego: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning, plus granular RBAC. Roles can be mapped to groups from IdP and we can enforce least privilege. There was a customer who wanted row-level access control — we don't do row-level in the platform yet, but you can combine RBAC with an access gateway in front of model endpoints.

[02:30] Marcus: How about audit logs — what events are logged, and can we ship logs to our SIEM or lock them down for 7 years?
[02:38] Priya (CSM): We capture token usage, API requests, model versions, rollouts, and role changes. We support streaming audit logs to customer S3 or SIEM via forwarders. Retention defaults are shorter in hosted; Dedicated and Private let you set retention and export.

[02:55] Sofia: Is the logs export tamper-evident? For audits we need integrity guarantees.
[03:00] Diego: We provide append-only audit logs with S3 object lock or can integrate with your log ingest and immutability controls. For Private on-prem you can point logs to your internal logging cluster.

[03:13] Elena: Data residency is critical — some EU and Canada deployments require data not to leave region. Can Redwood guarantee regional residency for hosted?
[03:22] Ava: For Hosted, we have regional endpoints but they are on our shared infra; we can regionally pin requests. For the strictest guarantees customers choose Dedicated in a region or Private VPC/on-prem where you control the network.

[03:36] Marcus: For Dedicated, is network egress fully controllable? We want to tightly restrict outbound.
[03:41] Diego: Yes, Dedicated allows egress policies and VPC peering or private links. We'll share a typical network diagram. There are also options for private endpoints and no public internet egress.

[03:55] Evan: We have strict data classification — any PHI must be encrypted in transit and at rest, and access logged. Do you do field-level encryption?
[04:04] Diego: We recommend encrypting sensitive fields before sending to the model if you need field-level guarantees. At infra-level, we encrypt in transit (TLS) and at rest using customer or Redwood-managed keys depending on deployment. For private, you can plug into your KMS.

[04:18] Elena: There's concern about model caching — will any user data be cached in a shared KV cache? We can't have PHI in shared caches.
[04:26] Diego: Good point. By default we have an LRU KV cache for performance. For PHI workloads, we can disable cross-customer caching or use customer-scoped caches. In Dedicated/Private we can enforce per-tenant caches only.

[04:40] Sofia: Retention policy — we need the ability to set retention per dataset and handle legal holds. Is that supported?
[04:47] Priya: Yes, for Private and Dedicated you can define retention windows per-route and apply legal hold flags. Hosted has default retention; we can discuss a contractual addendum if needed.

[04:58] Marcus: From an ops perspective, if we do Private (VPC), what's the upgrade/rollout model? How are patches applied? We need controlled maintenance windows.
[05:06] Diego: Private offers a customer-controlled control plane in your VPC. For on-prem we provide an upgrade bundle and can coordinate maintenance. For hosted/dedicated we have rolling upgrades; we can set blackout windows via SLA agreements.

[05:20] Elena: For compliance, do you provide evidence artifacts — e.g., system diagrams, encryption cipher lists, key rotation policy?
[05:27] Ava: Yes — our security pack includes network diagrams, encryption specs, key rotation cadence, SOC2 controls narrative. I'll attach that to the follow-up email.

[05:36] Sofia: A few nitty gritty Qs: Is SAML assertion lifetime configurable? Can we force MFA? Does RBAC have session timeouts?
[05:44] Diego: SAML assertion lifetime is configurable via the IdP; we support MFA enforcement through SSO (Okta, Azure). Session timeouts and idle session controls are configurable for enterprise customers.

[05:55] Elena: We're also evaluating latency/cost tradeoffs — if we run models in Private on-prem, what's the perf hit vs Redwood-hosted?
[06:03] Diego: Latency mainly depends on hardware and network topology. Our serving runtime supports same optimizations across deployments, but on-prem performance depends on your GPU types and kernel support. We can run a benchmark with your hardware profile to measure p99 and throughput.

[06:18] Marcus: Do you support quantized models or custom model builds? We may want int8 to save cost.
[06:23] Diego: Yes — runtime supports quantization profiles and we can onboard custom models. For private deployments we can load quantized binaries tuned to your hardware.

[06:34] Elena: About breach notification and incident response — what's SLA and process?
[06:39] Ava: We have a defined incident response plan, 72-hour notification for data incidents, and an incident commander model. For enterprise customers we can agree a faster notification timeline in contract.

[06:52] Evan: One more: network egress proofs for audits — can you provide attestations that no egress occurred outside allowed endpoints?
[06:58] Diego: We can provide egress logs and network flow records for the audit period; in Private you can centralize that in your logging stack. For Dedicated we can provide VPC flow logs as artifacts.

[07:10] Elena: Ok, sounds promising. A few follow-ups from legal: they want to see the SOC2 Type II report redacted and encryption key management details before we proceed.
[07:18] Ava: We'll share redacted SOC2 and the KMS integration doc. I'll also include sample contract language for data residency and retention.

[07:25] Sofia: Also want to schedule a technical deep dive with Marcus and Diego — specifically p99 tests and a plan to run a small PoC in our staging.
[07:33] Marcus: Yes, we want a PoC for two weeks: ingest pipeline, inference latency targets (p50 < 120ms, p99 < 400ms), and audit export validation.

[07:44] Diego: That works. I'll draft a PoC scope: test harness, dataset size, concurrency profile, success criteria.

[07:51] Elena: We'll also need to include legal for contract terms around data deletion and certs of destruction after retention window.

[07:58] Ava: Understood. We'll prepare a retention/deletion playbook and proposed contract language.

[08:05] Evan: Practical note — does Redwood provide terraform or IaC modules for Private deployment?
[08:10] Diego: Yes, we have Terraform modules and Helm charts for on-prem/K8s installs and arm/amp support. We'll share the repo access for sandbox testing.

[08:20] Elena: Anything else we should call out?
[08:23] Sofia: One more on legal holds: we need a mechanism to prevent deletion when a hold is active, and a clear audit trail of who put the hold.
[08:30] Priya: That's supported — holds are flagged and retained, and we capture change events in audit logs with actor identity.

[08:38] Ava: Quick recap — we'll send SOC2 certs, KMS integration and network diagram, draft PoC scope, and proposed contract clauses for retention and residency. Customer to share data classification and retention windows.
[08:51] Elena: Sounds good. Let's aim to reconvene after the SOC package is reviewed; Marcus and Diego will run the PoC planning sync.

[09:01] Ava: Great, I'll send meeting notes and the security pack. Thanks everyone.
[09:05] (call ends)

Notes about transcription quality: names occasionally garbled (Evan transcribed as Even in one snippet), acronyms sometimes phonetic ("sock two" for SOC2), and some technical words (KV cache) mis-transcribed as KV cash. Link references mentioned during call: https://redwood.example/security/soc2-summary.pdf (to be shared), https://redwood.example/docs/kms-integration, and a promised terraform repo link for Private deployment.

End of transcript.
